title: Fictional briefing: a library pilot and a workshop notice

sections.title: A small pilot suggests a question, not a causal conclusion
sections.text: In this fictional four-week pilot, electricity use was 8% lower across 12 rooms. The observation does not establish causation: weather and occupied hours were not controlled. A matched comparison could separate a schedule effect from these other explanations. The current evidence supports further testing, not general rollout.

segments.text: This is a fictional demonstration, not a real inbox or research report. We reviewed three sample messages: two newsletters and one notice. Coverage is partial, and older reminders have not been checked.

segments.title: Pilot and next question
segments.text: A fictional four-week library pilot recorded eight percent lower electricity use across twelve rooms. This small observation cannot establish that the new schedule caused the change; weather and occupancy may also matter. The useful next step is a matched comparison, rather than an immediate expansion. Would the difference remain after matching weather and occupied hours? A new comparison that removes the apparent benefit would change our judgment.

segments.title: Sample notice
segments.text: One fictional workshop notice gives a January twentieth registration deadline. The suggested action is to verify the date with the organizer before making plans. This example has no real registration link or obligation. Historical reminders remain unchecked, so this is a partial review.

stories.question: Does the sample pilot support expanding the new schedule?
stories.judgment: The small observation supports another comparison, not a general rollout.
stories.mechanism: Weather and occupancy can change electricity use independently of the schedule.
stories.implication: Match measurement periods and occupied hours before expanding the pilot.
stories.counterargument: The schedule may have contributed, and a cheap follow-up can still be worthwhile.
stories.would_change_mind: A matched comparison that eliminates the difference would remove support for a schedule effect.
